question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $3-\sqrt{2w+5}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $3-\sqrt{2w+5},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{4w}{3+\sqrt{2w+5}} & = \\ -\frac{4w}{3+\sqrt{2w+5}}\cdot \frac{3-\sqrt{2w+5}}{3-\sqrt{2w+5}} & = \\ -\frac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{(3+\sqrt{2w+5})(3-\sqrt{2w+5})} & = \\ -\frac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{{3}^{2}-(\sqrt{2w+5})^{2}} & = \\ -\frac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{9-(2w+5)} & = \\ -\frac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{4-2w} & = \\ -\frac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{2(2-w)} & = \\ -\frac{2w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{2-w}\end{aligned}
$$
